A board advertises a 16-bit analog input. This experiment finds out how many
of those bits carry information, how far the zero and the scale are from
nominal, and whether the timestamps on the samples describe the sampling grid
that was requested.

It is the first experiment on this site because every later uncertainty budget
quotes its results: the effective resolution of the converter, and the quality
of the sampling grid, are inputs to the thermal and mechanical experiments
just as much as to S2 and S3.

## What you measure {#sec-s1-index-measure}

| Quantity | How | Where it is used later |
|---|---|---|
| Offset and gain error | Three-point calibration against a DMM | Every voltage measurement on this site |
| Noise floor $\sigma$ | Repeated readings of a constant input, and of a shorted input | The Type A term of every budget |
| Effective number of bits | $\log_2\left(\mathrm{FSR}/(\sqrt{12}\,\sigma)\right)$ | The quantization term of every budget; compared with S2's dynamic ENOB |
| Sampling-grid quality | Least-squares grid fit of the device timestamps | S2's timing penalty, S3's aliasing, M3's modal analysis |
| Host dependence | The same acquisition on two hosts | The recommendation of which host to run a bench on |

: What S1 produces {#tbl-s1-index-outputs}

## Bench {#sec-s1-index-bench}

**Tier 1.** A supported board, a USB cable and a hub, a voltage reference IC,
two resistors and a digital multimeter. No signal generator, no oscilloscope.

**Board.** The static measurements work on any supported board. The timestamp
analysis needs streaming, which the Renesas boards (UNO R4 Minima, Nano R4)
do not have — see [Supported boards](../../setup/boards.qmd).

**Host.** Linux is recommended, and one of the experiment's results is the
evidence for that recommendation.

## Reference data {#sec-s1-index-data}

Five generated runs ship with the experiment, in `data/`:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `cal-0v`, `cal-1v25`, `cal-2v50` | 200 records each at 1 kHz, one channel, at the three calibration points |
| `noise-linux` | 5 s at 1 kHz, reference and shorted channel, Linux host |
| `noise-macos` | The same acquisition, macOS host |

: Reference data shipped with S1 {#tbl-s1-index-data}

::: {.callout-warning}
## The reference data is synthetic

It is produced by a seeded generator (`tools/synth/s1_daq_static.py`) whose
parameters are plausible placeholders, not measurements — they are marked
`TODO (Paolo)` in `tools/synth/params/`. It exists so the analysis templates
render, and are checked in continuous integration, with no hardware attached.
Every page that uses it says so.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="instructor"}
## Instructor summary {.instructor-note}

Three hours, tier 1, no prerequisites — this is the session to run first, and
the one where the effective-bits result does the most teaching. Full notes,
expected values, common failures and the rubric are in the
[handbook](handbook.qmd#sec-s1-instructor).
:::
